title: SLO-aware retry, hedging, and multi-region failover contract
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define a cross-service and SDK contract for retries, timeouts, backoff, idempotency keys, hedged requests, and multi-region failover so services can meet SLOs without creating duplicate work or surprising client behavior.
background: Multiple teams have implemented ad-hoc retry and hedging strategies which causes inconsistent behavior across SDKs and service endpoints: duplicated requests, uneven load during partial outages, and difficulty attributing SLO violations. We need a single, minimal contract that balances latency SLOs with safety for non-idempotent operations and enables reliable multi-region failover.
goals: 1) Provide a default retry and backoff policy usable by all SDKs and services. 2) Specify when and how hedged requests may be used. 3) Define idempotency key behavior for non-idempotent endpoints. 4) Establish circuit-breaker and load-shedding thresholds and signals. 5) Define observability signals required to validate SLO compliance.
non_goals: 1) Force all services to adopt exactly the same implementation detail (libraries may differ). 2) Replace business-level dedup workflows where application-level dedup is already required.
proposal_summary: Introduce a two-layer contract: a default platform RetryPolicy + Backoff template and an opt-in HedgingPolicy. Services must declare idempotency semantics in their API surface. SDKs will expose simple primitives (RetryPolicy, HedgingPolicy, IdempotencyKey) and honor server-provided hints. Multi-region failover uses ordered region preferences with transparent idempotency enforcement to prevent duplicates.
retry_backoff_spec: Defaults: - Max attempts: 3 for idempotent calls, 0 for non-idempotent unless idempotency key is present. - Base delay: 50ms, multiplier: 2.0, max delay: 5s. - Jitter: full jitter as described in AWS backoff (random between 0 and calculated delay). - Total attempt timeout: cap at 12s by default. SDKs should make this configurable but default to these platform values. Services can override per-route with documented rationale.
idempotency_spec: All mutating endpoints must declare whether they are: idempotent-by-design, idempotent-with-key, or non-idempotent. - If 'idempotent-with-key', clients must provide Idempotency-Key header (UUID v4 recommended). - Server must return Idempotency-Status header: one of (accepted, replayed, conflict). - Idempotency records must be stored durable for at least 24 hours for platform routes; long-lived enterprise routes may increase retention. - For multi-region failover, idempotency keys must be globally resolvable either via global storage or by including region-aware routing hints in the key (deterministic hashing is an allowed approach).
hedging_spec: Hedging allowed only for read-like or strongly idempotent operations and by explicit opt-in. Default hedging policy: - Max concurrent hedges: 2 (original + 1 hedged). - Hedge delay gap: 80ms. - Clients should cancel outstanding hedged requests on first successful response. - Hedging introduces a duplicate-detection contract: if hedging is enabled, servers are expected to be tolerant of near-simultaneous duplicate requests for the same idempotency key.
circuit_breaker_spec: Circuit breakers operate at region-service-route granularity. Default parameters: - Sliding window: 60s split into 12 buckets. - Error threshold: 15% error rate over window triggers open. - Minimum requests: 30 requests window. - Open duration: 30s with exponential open backoff (x2) up to 5 minutes. - Half-open probe: 5 requests. - State transition events must be emitted to tracing/metrics with reason codes (error_rate, instance_down, overload).
load_shedding: Platform load-shedding policy: - Each runtime exposes an optional Accept-Drop hint header to upstreams. - Soft threshold: 85% util => start token-based shedding of low-priority traffic. - Hard threshold: 95% util => aggressive shedding across non-critical routes. - Dropped requests should return 429 with Retry-After and a Shed-Reason header. - SDKs should surface a standardized exception type for dropped requests to allow client-side backoff and reduced retry attempts.
multi_region_failover: Failover rules: - Primary region preferred for low-latency. - If regional SLO (p99 latency or availability) degrades beyond configured limits or capacity signals indicate sustained queueing, route to secondary region. - Failover must preserve idempotency guarantees: clients must use Idempotency-Key and the platform will either forward key lookups to the primary idempotency store or write with causally-consistent semantics. - DNS or routing fallback alone is insufficient: we require observable routing decisions with trace/span tags (region=, failover_reason=) so customers can attribute costs and latency.
sdk_contract: SDKs must: 1) Expose a RetryPolicy object with fields (max_attempts, base_delay_ms, multiplier, max_delay_ms, total_timeout_ms). 2) Expose HedgingPolicy (enabled, max_hedges, hedge_delay_ms). 3) Provide convenience wrappers that attach Idempotency-Key for supported mutating calls. 4) Honor server-sent Retry-Suggest headers and adjust client behavior when server indicates temporary overload. 5) Provide telemetry hooks for retries, hedges, dropped requests, and duplicate detections.
service_changes: Services must: 1) Annotate APIs with idempotency semantics in OpenAPI/IDL. 2) Emit idempotency and duplicate metrics. 3) Support Idempotency-Key header and Idempotency-Status responses. 4) Accept and emit platform retry/hedge hints. 5) Implement regional circuit-breaking per above defaults or document overrides.
observability: Required metrics: retries_attempted (counter, tags: service, route, reason), hedged_invocations (counter), duplicate_requests_detected (counter), idempotency_misses (counter), shed_drops (counter, tags: priority), circuit_state_changes (counter with from->to), regional_failovers (counter, tags: primary, secondary, reason), p99_latency_by_route (histogram). Tracing: include retry/hedge spans with original request id and idempotency key. Dashboards: SLO panel per service showing user-facing p99, availability, retries per successful request, duplicate rate.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): publish spec, SDK reference impls for Go and Python, and server middleware templates. Phase 2 (4 weeks): opt-in pilot with 3 services (console-api, embeddings-store, runtime-orchestration). Phase 3 (4 weeks): enable default retry/backoff in SDKs for internal services and gate externally-facing endpoints behind feature flags. Phase 4: deprecate legacy client-side ad-hoc policies and require declaration in service IDLs.
testing_plan: Unit tests for SDK policies, integration tests simulating transient errors and hedging duplicates, chaos tests for region failover, load tests to validate shedding thresholds, and golden runs to ensure no duplicate side-effects for mutating operations under hedging+failover scenarios.
migration_steps: 1) Inventory routes and mark idempotency semantics. 2) Add Idempotency-Key support and emit Idempotency-Status. 3) Integrate platform SDK defaults behind flags. 4) Run pilot and collect telemetry for 2 weeks, iterate. 5) Gradual enforcement: require idempotency declaration in IDLs and reject routes missing annotations.
risks: 1) Incorrect idempotency declarations could cause silent data corruption. 2) Hedging increases tail resource usage and may worsen cost under heavy traffic if not controlled. 3) Multi-region idempotency store may add latency and complexity. 4) Divergent per-service overrides could reintroduce inconsistency.
open_questions: Should idempotency storage be global (single service) or federated with causal writes?
What is the minimum acceptable idempotency record retention for compliance customers?
Do we permit hedging for any customer-visible billing endpoints or restrict to internal-only?
How will enterprise private deployments configure global idempotency when air-gapped?
